questions.explanation: Bengal Tiger (Panthera tigris tigris) — national animal since 1973. Project Tiger launched in 1973.

questions.explanation: Indian Peacock (Pavo cristatus) — national bird. Also called national bird since 1963. Protected under Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.

questions.stem: The national tree of India is:
questions.explanation: Banyan tree — national tree. Represents immortality and long life. The Thimmamma Marrimanu in Andhra Pradesh is the world's largest single banyan tree.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.explanation: Lotus — national flower. Symbol of purity, beauty, and divinity. Grows in muddy water yet blooms spotlessly.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The national river of India is:
questions.explanation: Ganga was declared India's national river in 2008 by PM Manmohan Singh. Namami Gange Programme (2015) allocated Rs 20,000 crore to clean the Ganga.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

options.option_text: Ganges River Dolphin (South Asian river dolphin)

questions.explanation: Ganges River Dolphin (Platanista gangetica) — national aquatic animal since 2009. Critically endangered; nearly blind. Found in the Ganga-Brahmaputra river system.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.explanation: Bharat Ratna: India's highest civilian honour. Instituted in 1954. First recipient: C. Rajagopalachari, S. Radhakrishnan, C.V. Raman. B.R. Ambedkar received it posthumously in 1990.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: India has how many Union Territories (as of 2024)?
questions.explanation: 8 Union Territories: Delhi (NCT), Puducherry, J&K, Ladakh, Chandigarh, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu (merged 2020), Lakshadweep, Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The first woman President of India was:
questions.explanation: Pratibha Patil: 12th President of India (2007-2012), first woman. Draupadi Murmu is the 15th President (2022-) — first tribal woman President.

questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru: PM from 15 August 1947 until his death on 27 May 1964 — India's longest-serving PM (16+ years).

questions.stem: India's national motto 'Satyameva Jayate' (Truth Alone Triumphs) is taken from which ancient text?

options.option_text: Chandogya Upanishad (one of the principal Upanishads)
Brihadaranyaka Upanishad (the largest of all Upanishads)
Mundaka Upanishad (part of the Atharva Veda tradition)
Mandukya Upanishad (the shortest of all 108 Upanishads)

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'Satyameva Jayate' is drawn from Mundaka Upanishad (verse 3.1.6), one of the principal Upanishads belonging to the Atharva Veda. India adopted it as the national motto on 26 January 1950. Chandogya Upanishad (Option A) is a common wrong answer because it is longer and better known, but it contains a different set of philosophical dialogues and does not carry this phrase.

questions.stem: The State Emblem of India is an adaptation of the Lion Capital of Ashoka, originally located at which site?

options.option_text: Sanchi, Madhya Pradesh (famous for the Great Buddhist Stupa)
Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh (site of Buddha's first sermon, Dhammacakkappavattana)
Bodh Gaya, Bihar (where Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment)
Vaishali, Bihar (site of a tall Ashokan single-lion pillar)

questions.explanation: B is correct: The four-lion capital at Sarnath (Deer Park, Uttar Pradesh) was erected by Emperor Ashoka to commemorate the spot where the Buddha delivered his first sermon. India adopted this capital as its State Emblem in 1950. Vaishali (Option D) is a plausible distractor because it also has a famous Ashokan pillar, but that pillar bears only a single lion, not the four-lion abacus that inspired the emblem.

questions.stem: The 'Phulkari' embroidery tradition — characterised by dense geometric thread-work on coarse fabric — has received a Geographical Indication (GI) tag associated with which state?

options.option_text: Punjab, where thread is densely embroidered on khaddar or chiffon base
Haryana, known for its distinctive Phag needlework tradition instead
Rajasthan, famous for Kashida and Gota Patti embroidery art forms
Gujarat, renowned for Patola silk weaving and Bandhani tie-dye work

questions.explanation: A is correct: Phulkari (literally 'flower work') is a folk embroidery from Punjab in which coloured silk or woollen thread is worked on hand-spun khaddar. It received a GI tag under Punjab. Haryana (Option B) is the most tempting distractor because Phulkari is also practised in border districts of Haryana, but the GI tag and cultural origin are firmly associated with Punjab, not Haryana's distinct Phag needlework.

questions.stem: India's very first product to receive a Geographical Indication (GI) tag under the GI of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999 was?

options.option_text: Kancheepuram Silk Saree from Tamil Nadu (registered in 2005)
Darjeeling Tea from West Bengal (India's first GI tag, granted in 2004)
Mysore Sandal Soap from Karnataka (GI registration obtained in 2005)
Alphonso Mango from Ratnagiri, Maharashtra (GI registration obtained 2018)

questions.explanation: B is correct: Darjeeling Tea was granted India's first GI tag (Registration No. 1) in 2004, even before Kancheepuram Silk and Mysore Sandal Soap which followed in 2005. Kancheepuram Silk (Option A) is a common wrong answer because it is a high-profile GI product frequently cited, but it was registered after Darjeeling Tea.

questions.stem: The 'Garba' dance form of India was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2023. It belongs to which state and is primarily associated with which festival?

options.option_text: Rajasthan, performed as part of Teej and Desert Festival celebrations
Maharashtra, associated with Ganesh Chaturthi and Gudi Padwa festivities
Madhya Pradesh, linked to Karma Puja and tribal harvest ceremonies
Gujarat, performed in concentric circles during the nine nights of Navratri

questions.explanation: D is correct: Garba is intrinsic to Gujarat's Navratri celebration, where dancers move in concentric circles around a central lamp or idol of Goddess Amba. UNESCO inscribed it in December 2023. Rajasthan (Option A) is the most tempting distractor because it has its own vibrant folk dances (Ghoomar, Kalbelia), and some students confuse the two states' traditions.

questions.stem: The 'Dokra' (Dhokra) art tradition uses the lost-wax (cire perdue) casting technique and is practised by tribal artisans primarily across which cluster of Indian states?

options.option_text: Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Maharashtra (the western metalcraft corridor)
Manipur, Nagaland, and Assam (the northeastern bronze-casting region)
West Bengal, Odisha, and Chhattisgarh (the traditional Dhokra heartland)
Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana (the Deccan metal craft region)

questions.explanation: C is correct: The Dhokra (Dokra) tradition is concentrated in Bankura and West Midnapore (West Bengal), Bastar (Chhattisgarh), and parts of Odisha — all within the Gondwana tribal belt. The art predates the Harappan civilisation and uses beeswax and clay moulds. Manipur/Nagaland (Option B) is the most plausible distractor because the northeast has its own bronze-casting traditions, but those are distinct techniques and communities, not the Dokra tradition specifically.

questions.stem: The 'Wangala' — the grandest harvest festival of the Garo tribe of Meghalaya — is celebrated as a thanksgiving to which deity, who is believed to have bestowed fertility and good harvest upon the community?

options.option_text: Saljong — the Sun deity of fertility and agricultural abundance
Bwrai Bathou — the supreme primordial deity of the Bodo community
U Blei Nongthaw — the all-pervading creator deity of the Khasi people
Haram and Abge — the first man and woman in Santali cosmological belief

questions.explanation: A is correct: Wangala (also called the '100 Drums Festival') is held by the Garo tribe in honour of Saljong, their Sun god associated with fertility, who grants a bountiful harvest. Bwrai Bathou (Option B) is the most tempting wrong answer because it is another well-known Northeast tribal deity, but Bathou is the deity of the Bodo tribe of Assam — a different community. Khasi (Option C) and Santali (Option D) traditions are also real, making all four options plausibly linked to Northeast/tribal cultures.
